profile.name: Jorge
profile.title: AI Engineer & AI Enabler · 25 years building software that people use
profile.description:
My job is to make AI useful, not just shiny, for people and for the product, from engineering to marketing, HR or sales.

I have been building and using AI every day for 5 years, and I have learned to keep it under control: tests, evals, security and, above all, measuring the impact. This is how I help take AI products to production, with observability and costs under control.

25 years of building software have taught me **not to trust nice demos** until I see them in production, with real users.

I like to share what I learn in talks and workshops, especially what does not work or what went wrong for us. 😅

In my personal life I am the father of 4 little dragons: the hardest project I have ever had, and with no rollback option.

details.name: stepwise-dev: development workflow for Claude Code
details.description:
Open source plugins for Claude Code, which also work with Codex, to keep the context under control with a **Research → Plan → Implement → Validate** workflow: /clear between phases, and everything researched and planned is saved in files so it is not lost.

It includes skills for good practices such as TDD, small safe steps, story splitting or the hamburger method, and a research system with several agents.

The main skills have **evals** to check that they add something more than what the model already does on its own.

[Article: Your CLAUDE.md does not work (without Context Engineering)](https://nikeyes.github.io/tu-claude-md-no-funciona-sin-context-engineering-es/)

details.name: Speaker at AWS Summit Madrid 2026: Boost your productivity with Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock
details.description:
I presented the real case of Kleinanzeigen:
- From 0 to 350 people using Claude Code.
- 340 repositories migrated to Java 25 autonomously.
- A PR reviewer with our own rules.
- Governance with Bedrock and impact metrics, not only usage metrics.

And most important: everything that is not working for us. 😅

details.name: I trust my skills because they have evals
details.description:
There are hundreds of skills for Claude Code, but I use very few: only the ones that prove they add something more than what the model already does by default.

I explain how I measure them with the skill-creator evaluation framework: the same task with and without the skill, comparing pass rate, tokens and time in each iteration.

**Evals are the tests of your skills.** Without them you do not know if they work: you only believe they work.

details.name: Talk and workshop: Developing with AI - Discovering better ways to develop
details.description:
Talk and hands-on workshop about AI-assisted software development, given at Wallbox, Adevinta and Kleinanzeigen.

The talk starts from the METR study, where senior developers believed they were 20% faster with AI but were actually 19% slower. The main idea: the problem is not AI, it is how we use it. I explain with practical examples how I use AI in my daily development work.

In the workshop each person works with Claude Code on their own repo and a real ticket: CLAUDE.md and context, permissions, hooks as guardrails, skills, subagents and plugins.

[Material and slides](https://github.com/nikeyes/ai-dev-workshop)

details.name: Your CLAUDE.md does not work (without Context Engineering)
details.description:
Why Claude Code ends up ignoring your CLAUDE.md after a while: the problem is not your rules, it is the context. The context window is not the attention window, and after 60% the quality drops.

I explain the **Research → Plan → Implement → Validate** workflow, with `/clear` between phases and the knowledge saved in files, and how I automated it in [stepwise-dev](https://github.com/nikeyes/stepwise-dev).

details.name: How to be in the 5% that does get value from generative AI
details.description:
95% of generative AI projects fail. In this article I explain what makes the other 5% different.

- **Before you start:** when it makes sense to use AI and when an if/else is enough.
- **The most common mistakes:** POC after POC without reaching production, "we will optimize later" and not specializing the AI in your domain.
- **How to do it right:** business metrics from day 1, observability and evals, simple architecture, costs under control and accuracy where it matters.

With real cases such as Lumen, Vodafone or LawGeex.

manfredSpecificData.desiredJobDescription:
I see myself in an **AI Engineer** or **AI Enabler** role where I can build products and, at the same time, help the whole organization, technical and non-technical, get the most out of AI.

I fit well in companies that want to take AI to production and to their teams, not just experiment with it. Places that trust autonomy, allow failing in order to learn, and do not forget that technology is a useful servant but a dangerous master.

Work-life balance is essential for me: my biggest passion is my family, and balance lets me give my best both at work and at home.
manfredSpecificData.goodPractices:
I believe in agile methodologies, but not without the technical practices that let us deliver software faster and with better quality:
- Simple design
- TDD and automated tests
- Refactoring
- Pair programming
- Continuous integration and delivery

With AI I do the same: tests, evals and small steps, to know that something works, not just believe it.

**I am pragmatic**: I know when to relax the practices to **reach the user sooner**, fix a problem in production or validate a hypothesis.

**I love learning**, and anyone on the team can teach me something, whether they have been here one year or twenty.
